citations.assessment: The Mishnah expressly names Menaḥem ben Sagnai and records his testimony about the vessels of olive boilers and dyers.

The last chapter’s parallel gives the same testimony, seating at the academy and the others’ astonishment. It reads ben Povgi and adds that he was a dyer. The precise causal connection to the appointment is Heilprin’s phrasing.

holds.reason: Gamliel is named in the preceding mishnah and Neḥunya ben Gudgada in the following mishnah. These neighboring notices do not alone establish the stated contemporary relationship or identify Yoḥanan with Neḥunya.
